_about: Topic backlog for the daily episode task. It takes the first 'next' entry, then marks it 'queued'. See content/DAILY_EPISODE_GUIDE.md.

topics.title: How deep is the Mariana Trench, really?
topics.angle: Sinking 11 km to Challenger Deep.

topics.title: What if you fell into a hole through the Earth?
topics.angle: The fall takes only 38 minutes, and you'd swing back and forth forever.

topics.title: What if you started floating up and couldn't stop?
topics.angle: The thermosphere tops 1,000 degrees, but you'd freeze.

topics.title: What if you sank all the way down to the Titanic?
topics.angle: 3.8 km down in the dark; the twist is that bacteria are eating the wreck and it may be gone within decades.

topics.title: How big is the biggest star?
topics.angle: Moon → Earth → Jupiter → Sun → Betelgeuse → UY Scuti; twist: put Betelgeuse where the Sun is and you'd live inside it.

topics.title: What if you lined up every planet?
topics.angle: Mercury → Mars → Venus → Earth → Neptune → Uranus → Saturn → Jupiter; twist: all the planets would fit in the gap between Earth and the Moon.

topics.title: What's the highest thing that can fly?
topics.angle: Rise past a vulture at 11 km, the SR-71, weather balloons, meteors burning up, to Hubble; the twist is that a bird has hit a plane at 11 km.

topics.title: Some moons are bigger than planets
topics.angle: Our Moon → Europa → Titan → Mercury → Ganymede; twist: Ganymede and Titan are both wider than the planet Mercury.

topics.title: What if you fell into a hole through the Moon?
topics.angle: Through regolith, crust and mantle to a small iron core; the twist is the fall takes longer than on Earth despite the Moon being smaller.

topics.title: How small is Earth, really?
topics.angle: Earth → Sun → Sirius → Arcturus → Rigel → Antares; hook: you think Earth is big? Watch this.

topics.title: Follow a whale on the deepest dive of any mammal
topics.angle: A Cuvier's beaked whale holds its breath almost 3 km down; the twist is how long it stays under.

topics.title: The planets that got demoted
topics.angle: Ceres → Makemake → Eris → Pluto → our Moon; twist: Pluto is smaller than our Moon.

topics.title: What's under 4 km of Antarctic ice?
topics.angle: Drill down through ice layers that are hundreds of thousands of years old to a lake sealed off for millions of years (Lake Vostok).

topics.title: What if you sank to the bottom of the deepest lake?
topics.angle: Lake Baikal is 1.6 km deep and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water; the twist is the animals found nowhere else.

topics.title: What if you fell into a hole through Mars?
topics.angle: Through a dusty crust and mantle to a liquid core; compare the fall time and top speed with Earth's.

topics.title: What's at the bottom of the ocean under the North Pole?
topics.angle: Below 2 m of sea ice, 4 km down to where a flag was planted by submersible in 2007.

topics.title: How big is the biggest volcano in the solar system?
topics.angle: Tour Mars from Olympus Mons to Valles Marineris and Hellas basin; the twist is that Olympus Mons is so wide its edge would sit below the horizon if you stood at the top.

topics.title: What if you could see like a bee?
topics.angle: Bees see ultraviolet patterns on flowers; your cones could too if your lens didn't block UV; twist: Monet lost a lens in 1923 and his lilies turned blue-purple.

topics.title: What if you climbed down the deepest cave on Earth?
topics.angle: Down Veryovkina Cave in Abkhazia, over 2 km deep, past shafts and flooded sumps; the twist is that cavers spend weeks underground to reach the bottom.

topics.title: Could Saturn really float in water?
topics.angle: Spin round Saturn, its rings and the hexagon storm at the north pole; the twist is that its average density is lower than water's.

topics.title: What if you could see with sound, like a bat?
topics.angle: You wake up with echolocation: clicks, echoes, catching insects in the dark; the twist is that some blind people really do learn to echolocate with tongue clicks.

topics.title: Is there more water on Europa than on Earth?
topics.angle: A cracked ice moon of Jupiter hiding a salty ocean; the twist is that it may hold about twice the water of all Earth's oceans.

topics.title: How big are asteroids, really?
topics.angle: From small asteroids like Bennu up to Vesta and Ceres, then our Moon; the twist is how small the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs was next to them.

topics.title: What if you sank into the deepest blue hole?
topics.angle: Down the deepest known blue hole, Taam Ja' off Mexico, where the water loses its oxygen; the twist is that divers and sonar still haven't found its bottom.

topics.title: How big is Jupiter's Great Red Spot?
topics.angle: Spin round Jupiter to a storm that has raged for centuries and is wider than Earth; the twist is that it has been shrinking.

topics.title: What if you rode a balloon to the edge of space?
topics.angle: Rise with Alan Eustace's 2014 balloon to about 41 km, past airliners and the ozone layer, then jump; the twist is that he broke the sound barrier on the way down.

topics.title: What if you could see heat, like a snake?
topics.angle: You wake up sensing warmth in the dark like a pit viper, spotting warm bodies at night; the twist is how small a temperature change those pits can detect.

topics.title: How big can planets get?
topics.angle: From Earth to Neptune, Jupiter and the biggest known puffy exoplanets; the twist is that some giant planets are wider than Jupiter but lighter than it.

topics.title: What if you sank to a deep-sea volcano vent?
topics.angle: Down to black smokers on the sea floor where water comes out hotter than boiling but doesn't boil; the twist is the life that lives on chemicals, not sunlight.

topics.title: What if you rode a rocket to the space station?
topics.angle: Rise past clouds, the ozone layer and the edge of space to the ISS about 400 km up; the twist is that you'd get there in a matter of hours, faster than many flights across an ocean.
